title: Sorgho-tchap (Sorghum and Bean Stew, Northern Cameroon)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Red sorghum grains cooked about an hour, red or black beans about 1½ hours, then both simmered 5 minutes in the fried onion and spice base.
longDesc: p. 20 of the October 2023 recipe book: 1 kg of red sorghum and 750 g of red or black beans, with the same seasonings as Corn-tchap. The sorghum is cooked about an hour and the beans about 1 hour 30; both go into the fried base and simmer 5 minutes. The final step as printed mentions a ‘mélange maïs-haricot’, evidently a carry-over from the maize recipe.
ingredients: Oil, tomato, bell pepper, white pepper, onion, parsley, celery, basil, garlic, ginger, salt, chilli, stock cube, rock salt — quantities not printed
steps: Cook the sorghum in water with rock salt about an hour. Cool and wash.
Cook the beans in salted water about 1 hour 30. Wash them.
Chop the onion and bell pepper; crush the other condiments.
Roast the onion, add the crushed condiments and simmer. Season with salt and the stock cube.
Add the sorghum and beans and simmer 5 minutes. Serve.
chefTips: Same pattern as Corn-tchap with sorghum in place of maize.
The final step on the page mentions a maize-bean mix — a copy error in the source.
commonMistakes: Taking the maize-bean wording in the last step literally.
healthBenefits: Sorghum and beans give complex carbohydrate, protein and fibre.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Sorgho-tchap’ (p. 20). Authors as printed: ‘Tata Ngome et al.’ (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré; ReSI-NoC project); October 2023 (V1), © 2024, CC BY 4.0. Yield not printed for any recipe in the book. Servings 8 and prep are placeholders. Quantities and times TWO-PASS; text SINGLE-PASS.
FLAG: the last step names a ‘mélange maïs-haricot’ in a sorghum recipe; reported as printed. ABSENT: seasoning quantities.
